newsitem.title: USA: Hinckley regrets shooting Reagan - father.
newsitem.headline: Hinckley regrets shooting Reagan - father.

text.p: John Hinckley greatly regrets trying to kill then-President Ronald Reagan in 1981 and should be granted his request to leave a mental hospital for unsupervised visits, his father said Wednesday.
"He is very, very regretful, he's terribly sorry for what he did and wishes there were some way he could undo it but he can't," Jack Hinckley said in an interview on NBC's "Today" programme.

His mother, Jo Ann, said in the interview: "Our son now is over his serious mental illness. He is well. He no longer has his psychosis, he is no longer depressed ... he's an entirely different person."

Hinckley has been held at St. Elizabeth's mental hospital in Washington since 1982 when he was acquitted on grounds of insanity of shooting Reagan and three others outside the Washington Hilton Hotel in 1981.
Reagan, a Secret Service agent and a police officer recovered from the attack, but Reagan press secretary James Brady was left critically wounded.
Hinckley is asking a federal court in Washington for at least the fourth time to grant him the right to make the 12-hour, unescorted visits. Prosecutors continue to oppose his request.
He and his lawyers begin Wednesday the third of what is expected to be four days of hearings before U.S. District Court Judge June Green.
Hinckley's father said his son should be granted his request because "freedom is everything and John's been working hard for 16 years to recover from this terrible illness.
"His doctors tell us that now he is recovered and he's ready for the next step. John is talented. He's not dumb, he's smart. He just was hit by this terrible mental illness."
Over the last decade Hinckley has been allowed to leave the hospital for court appearances only.
